instructions: Slice the onions into thin strips and the garlic thin. Cut the tuna into 3/4-inch cubes and pat dry. Season the tuna with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a very large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the onions with 1/2 tsp of the salt for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and starting to color.
Add the garlic, bay leaves and oregano and stir for 1 minute. Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds, then pour in the sherry. Cook 5 minutes, until the liquid has reduced. Scoop the onions into a bowl.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same pan over high heat. Sear the tuna 2 minutes, turn it and sear 1 minute, so the outside is browned and the middle is still pink. For fully cooked tuna, cook it 3 minutes in the next step instead.
Return the onions to the pan with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and toss with the tuna for 1 minute. Take the bay leaves out and serve right away.
method_notes: Directo al Paladar's Andalusian version (211 votes, no average shown) is the only one read in full, so it leads as a fallback. It cooks a pile of onions slowly with garlic, oregano and paprika, reduces sherry, and sears the tuna cubes quickly. It serves two, so the amounts are doubled, with five onions rather than six so the pan isn't overloaded. The oil quantity was missing from its list and comes from its steps.
